questions.question: What is the correct method to initialize the Braze SDK in an Android application?
options: Braze.getInstance(context) is used after initialization in braze.xml
questions.explanation: The Braze Android SDK is initialized through configuration in braze.xml, after which Braze.getInstance(context) is used to access the Braze instance. The SDK automatically initializes from the configuration file.

questions.question: Which method is correct for logging a custom event in the Braze Android SDK?
questions.explanation: The correct method to log a custom event in the Android SDK is Braze.getInstance(context).logCustomEvent(eventName), which logs the event to the current user's profile.

questions.question: True or False: Custom attributes in the Braze Android SDK must be set before a user is identified.
questions.explanation: Custom attributes can be set at any time and will be associated with the user once they are identified. There is no requirement to set them before identification.

questions.question: What does the changeUser() method do in the Braze Android SDK?
options: Identifies a user with a unique external user ID and creates a new user profile
Logs the user out of the app
questions.explanation: The changeUser() method identifies a user with a unique external user ID and creates or updates their user profile in Braze. This is essential for tracking individual users across sessions.

questions.question: Which data types are supported for custom event properties in the Braze Android SDK? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The Braze Android SDK supports String, int, float, boolean, and Date objects for custom event properties. Image is not a supported data type for event properties.

questions.question: Which interface should be implemented to custom handle deep links opened by Braze in Android?
questions.explanation: The IBrazeDeeplinkHandler interface should be implemented to custom handle all deep links opened by Braze across push notifications, in-app messages, and Content Cards in Android.

questions.question: In the Braze Android SDK, when should the BrazeDeeplinkHandler delegate be set?
questions.explanation: The BrazeDeeplinkHandler delegate should be set in your app's Application.onCreate() method in most cases, to ensure it's available early in the app lifecycle.

questions.question: What does the com_braze_handle_push_deep_links_automatically flag do in the Android SDK?
options: Controls whether tapping a push notification automatically brings the app to foreground and opens its deep link
questions.explanation: The com_braze_handle_push_deep_links_automatically flag in braze.xml controls whether the SDK automatically brings your app to the foreground and opens deep links when a push notification is tapped.

questions.question: True or False: The Braze Android SDK requires additional setup beyond basic SDK integration to display in-app messages.
questions.explanation: The Braze Android SDK handles in-app message display automatically after basic SDK integration. The default UI is provided out-of-the-box with no additional setup required.

questions.question: Which class is used to display Content Cards in the Braze Android SDK?
questions.explanation: The ContentCardsFragment class is used to display Content Cards in the Braze Android SDK. It's available in the Braze Android UI project and automatically handles display and analytics.

questions.question: Which method sets a custom attribute for the current user in the Braze Android SDK?
questions.explanation: In the Braze Android SDK (Kotlin), you use Braze.getInstance(context).currentUser?.setCustomUserAttribute(key, value) to set custom attributes. In Java, this would be accessed through the currentUser property.

questions.question: Can you log a purchase event in the Braze Android SDK?
options: No, only custom events are supported
Yes, using logPurchase() method with product ID, price, currency, and optional quantity
Yes, but only through the REST API
No, purchase tracking is not supported in Android SDK
questions.explanation: Yes, the Braze Android SDK supports logging purchase events using the logPurchase() method, which accepts product ID, price, currency code, quantity, and optional properties.

questions.question: True or False: User attributes set before calling changeUser() are automatically carried over to the new user profile.
questions.explanation: User attributes set before calling changeUser() are not automatically carried over. When you call changeUser() with a new external user ID, a new user profile is created, and previously set attributes are not transferred.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) in the context of Braze Android SDK?
options: To replace the Braze SDK entirely
To provide push notification tokens and handle push delivery to the Braze SDK
questions.explanation: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) provides push notification tokens and handles the delivery of push notifications to the Braze SDK, which then processes and displays them to users.

questions.question: Which of the following can you customize in Braze Android in-app messages? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: You can customize message styling, appearance, and dismissal behavior in Braze Android in-app messages. The device hardware cannot be customized, and message display timing is controlled by Braze campaigns.

questions.question: Where should the Braze API key be configured in the Android SDK?
questions.explanation: The Braze API key should be configured in the braze.xml configuration file located in the res/values directory of your Android project.

questions.question: True or False: Custom attribute keys in the Braze Android SDK are case-insensitive.
questions.explanation: Custom attribute keys are case-sensitive in Braze. You must use the exact same case when referencing them as you used when creating them.

questions.question: When should you call requestImmediateDataFlush() in the Braze Android SDK?
options: After every custom event to ensure immediate transmission
Only when the app is about to terminate or when immediate data syncing is critical
Never, the SDK handles data flushing automatically
Every time a user logs in
questions.explanation: You should call requestImmediateDataFlush() only when it's critical to sync data immediately, such as when the app is terminating or before a critical action. Regular calls can impact performance.

questions.question: What permissions are required in the Android Manifest for Braze push notifications?
options: All permissions are optional in Braze
questions.explanation: At minimum, android.permission.INTERNET and android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE are required for Braze to function properly with push notifications and data syncing.

questions.question: True or False: Content Cards in the Braze Android SDK automatically log analytics for impressions and clicks.
questions.explanation: Yes, the ContentCardsFragment automatically logs usage analytics for Content Cards, including impressions and clicks, without requiring additional code.

questions.question: Which method enables you to manually log an in-app message impression in the Braze Android SDK?
questions.explanation: You can manually log in-app message impressions using Braze.getInstance(context).logInAppMessageImpression(inAppMessage) when handling custom in-app message UI.

questions.question: What is a key-value pair in the context of Braze Android push notifications?
options: A way to encrypt push payloads
Custom key-value data that can be passed in a push notification and accessed by your app
A method to authenticate with Braze servers
A way to schedule push notifications
questions.explanation: Key-value pairs are custom data that can be included in push notifications and accessed by your app, allowing you to pass data and trigger custom behavior based on push content.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of custom events you can log in a single session?
questions.explanation: There is no maximum limit on the number of custom events you can log in a single session. The Braze Android SDK queues and batches events for transmission.

questions.question: True or False: It's recommended to set user IDs as soon as possible after app launch in the Braze Android SDK.
questions.explanation: Yes, it's a best practice to call changeUser() with the user's ID as soon as possible after app launch to ensure proper user tracking and attribution of events and attributes.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid data types for custom attributes in the Braze Android SDK? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: The Braze Android SDK supports String and numeric types (int, long, float/double) for custom attributes. File and XML are not valid custom attribute data types.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the class_type key-value pair in Braze Android Content Cards?
options: To determine how the card renders in your app
To schedule when the card displays
questions.explanation: The class_type key-value pair in Content Cards is used to determine how the card renders in your app, allowing you to display different card types with custom styling.

questions.question: What happens when you call changeUser() with the same user ID multiple times?
options: It creates a new user profile each time
It updates the existing user profile without creating duplicates
It logs an error in the console
questions.explanation: Calling changeUser() with the same user ID multiple times updates the existing user profile without creating duplicates. Braze tracks based on the unique external user ID.

questions.question: True or False: You can log button clicks in in-app messages using logInAppMessageClicked() in the Braze Android SDK.
questions.explanation: Yes, you can manually log in-app message button clicks using logInAppMessageClicked(inAppMessage) when implementing custom in-app message handling.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for handling sensitive data like passwords in custom attributes?
options: Store them as encrypted custom attributes
Never store sensitive data like passwords in custom attributes; use secure storage
Store them as string custom attributes with no encryption
Use the Braze API to encrypt them
questions.explanation: Never store sensitive data like passwords or tokens in Braze custom attributes. Use secure storage mechanisms provided by Android for sensitive information.

questions.question: In which lifecycle method should you typically initialize or configure Braze in your Application class?
questions.explanation: The Braze SDK should be configured in your Application class's onCreate() method to ensure it's initialized as early as possible in the app lifecycle.
